# Tugrul Guner

Canonical profile: https://tugrul.modepot.io/

Tugrul Guner is an AI Engineering Manager at CDAI in Toronto, Canada. He leads two cross-functional pods across a portfolio of more than six products. He builds high-performing teams and operates well under pressure, bringing structure to ambiguity and making difficult decisions without lowering engineering standards. He remains hands-on building scalable, robust backend, AI, and agentic systems designed to adapt as products, models, and infrastructure change.

He created ModePot, an open-source family of frameworks, tools, engines, and games built around simpler APIs, modern runtimes, performance, and explicit boundaries between deterministic software and agent-owned decisions.

He also contributes to Hermes Agent and Superpowers. His public work includes a merged Hermes Kanban reliability fix and submitted improvements across agent skills, harness support, MCP, and tooling. His experience spans agent orchestration, reusable skills, evaluation, low-level LLM optimization, backend architecture, and production infrastructure. He configures and orchestrates agents such as Hermes Agent and Claude Code with project context, reusable skills, executable tools, and clear boundaries. He designs workflows combining agent-driven decisions with deterministic software, delegates focused tasks, and verifies results through tests, review, and execution evidence.

## Technical range

- Agent harnesses: Hermes Agent and Claude Code are high-level agent environments configured with project context, tool access, and focused delegation; deepagents is a programmable agent-harness library for building custom agents.
- Agent and LLM application development: Pydantic AI for typed agents, LangGraph for stateful workflows and durable execution, and DSPy for composing and optimizing LLM programs.
- Skills, protocols, and tool integration: Superpowers is a collection of reusable software-development skills; MCP is the Model Context Protocol; FastMCP is the Python framework for implementing MCP servers and clients. Custom skill authoring and tool integration are capabilities, not additional framework names.
- Models and low-level inference: PyTorch, TensorFlow, Hugging Face, llama.cpp, vLLM; LLM inference optimization, quantization, and ONNX optimization.
- Model serving and ML operations: KServe, Ray Serve, LitServe, MLflow, Databricks; model deployment, experiment tracking, and production ML pipelines.
- Backend engineering: FastAPI, Django; API design, scalable backend architecture, and integration of models and agents into applications.
- Databases and messaging: PostgreSQL, DynamoDB, MongoDB, Qdrant, Redis, RabbitMQ; relational, key-value, document, and vector data systems, caching, and messaging.
- Languages, cloud, and delivery: Python, SQL, Bash; AWS, Azure, GCP; Docker, Kubernetes, Git, GitHub Actions.

## Story

Tugrul began coding and working with machine learning during his master's degree in 2012, learned traditional machine-learning approaches, participated in Kaggle competitions, and practiced feature engineering. He later used deep learning for computer vision with microscope images during his first postdoctoral appointment and for image reconstruction during his second. As the models became more capable, he became increasingly interested in the backends, deployment, infrastructure, and operating practices required to make AI reliable beyond an experiment. That path led him into MLOps and production AI. His earlier research in physics and materials science—30 journal publications, a patent, and more than 1,000 citations—shaped the analytical, evidence-led mindset he brings to innovation and uncertainty; it is not presented as AI research.

ModePot is where he builds tools and systems he wants to exist. Passionately Curious makes difficult scientific ideas accessible to broad audiences. His personal essays examine ambition, mortality, curiosity, and the future behind his work.

## Leadership ambition

As a manager, Tugrul is ambitious about creating high-performing teams where talented people take ownership and raise the standard for one another. He gives people the context and authority to make good decisions, with explicit ownership and standards that make autonomy work. He operates well under pressure, especially when timelines are tight, priorities are shifting, and difficult decisions cannot wait. He brings structure to ambiguity, makes the necessary tradeoffs, and keeps the team moving without lowering engineering standards. As he takes on greater organizational scope, he wants to stay close enough to the technology to make sound decisions while helping people grow into harder problems and challenge ideas with evidence.

## Writing

Tugrul created Passionately Curious because years in research showed him how much discovery stays buried in language written for specialists. The evidence-led newsletter brings questions from physics, AI, and biology to readers from any background by following the mechanism rather than summarizing papers and by keeping uncertainty visible. He has also published seven Medium essays about technology, scientific curiosity, ambition, mortality, and building the future. Two personal essays that describe his outlook are “Legacy Is Overrated. I Want to Be Alive for What Comes Next.” and “Nothing Is Waiting For Us. And That’s Why I Care.”
